title.narrative: Advocate ratification of the 1970 Convention and strengthening policy

description.narrative:
Efforts to combat illicit import, export, and transfer of ownership of cultural property need to be enhanced in Southern Africa particularly through the implementation of the 1970 Convention on the Means of Prohibiting and Preventing the Illicit Import, Export and Transfer of Ownership of Cultural Property. Namibia is yet to ratify the Convention, as part of reinforcing ratification two workshops were organised in Namibia at regional and national level in 2021 and 2022. The National workshop held in 2022 moved a motion for Namibia to ratify the 1970 Convention. As a follow up the Ministry of Education, Arts and Culture to initiate and lead the process of ratifying the Convention. Supporting Namibia to refine the Draft National Policy for the Repatriation of Human Remains and Restitution of Heritage Objects, as well as the National Guidelines for the Repatriation of Human Remains (and Associated Objects) and Restitution of Heritage Objects, and the National Guidelines for Handling and Managing Human Remains (and Associated Objects) and Heritage Objects.
Key Activities - Support Ministry of Education, Arts and Culture towards the ratification of the 1970 convention and for the refining of the policy and guidelines on repatriation and handling Human Remains (and Associated Objects) and Heritage Objects.
- Provide support towards the government led community consultations to refine the draft Policy on Human Remains and Artefacts as well as the drafting of guidelines on handling of Human remains and artefacts.
